text:
maria: anyone seeing a latency spike on private eu-west clusters? p50 jumped ~4x around 02:15 UTC, a bunch of customer requests timing out

 tj: yep saw it in the dashboards, throughput also down on the ded-*/private nodes :eyes:

 ashok: initial flamegraphs point at kernel fallback path in our runtime (kv kernel selector picked generic memcpy path) — KV lookup latency went from ~200us to 2-3ms when the spike started

 maria: I pulled the node level metrics. conntrack count shot up and NAT egress retransmits increased. suspecting ephemeral port starvation + heavy short-lived connections from a noisy tenant causing a noisy-neighbor egress storm

 leo: can you paste the conntrack dump?

 maria: sure, here's a small extract from the oncall node (redacted IPs):

 ```
 conntrack count: 196k
 # conntrack snippet
 tcp      6 431998 ESTABLISHED src=10.0.5.12 dst=3.121.45.6 sport=43412 dport=443 packets=234 bytes=18234 src=3.121.45.6 dst=10.0.5.12 sport=443 dport=43412 packets=220 bytes=17120
 tcp      6 431998 ESTABLISHED src=10.0.7.33 dst=52.15.23.48 sport=55678 dport=443 packets=54 bytes=4120
 ...
 ```

 infra-bot: autoscaler: scale-up triggered for private-eu-west-1 pool at 02:17 UTC (delta +3 nodes)

 tj: interesting — autoscaler added nodes but p50 stayed high. that usually means packet processing/egress path is the bottleneck, not CPU on the runtime pods themselves

 ashok: we also saw KV cache churn: eviction rate spiked concurrent with conntrack. possible causal chain: noisy tenant opens many short connections -> NAT table fills -> kernel starts fragmenting/deferring packets -> our runtime kernel selector falls back to slower memcpy path due to increased page faults under pressure -> batching windows shrink because requests get delayed and re-ordered -> per-token latency increases

 maria: here's a profiler snapshot from the runtime around the spike (sampling, 2s):

 ```
 # pprof text (top)
 30.5%  runtime  kernel_selector_fallback
 18.2%  runtime  kv_lookup_with_retries
 12.7%  net     tcp_retransmit
 8.9%   runtime  batching_window_adjustment::wait
 6.1%   user    user_callback
 ```

 leo: that kernel_selector_fallback is the kicker. it means we didn't choose the vectorized kernel for tokenization/attn op and fell back to safe path. we need to see why — usually because the kernel reported unsupported CPU features or memory layout changed (e.g., fragmented pages)

 tj: can you check dmesg / kernel logs for frag/oom/hugepage messages?

 maria: dmesg shows a lot of conntrack warnings and a couple of "nf_conntrack: table full" around 02:16. no OOM though.

 ashok: couple quick mitigation ideas:
 - increase conntrack hashsize / table size on nodes and extend ephemeral port range (sysctl)
 - enable connection reuse/pool at the egress proxy so runtime keeps fewer outbound sockets
 - temporarily pin kernel-selector to preferred kernel (force vectorized kernel) to see if latency improves
 - reduce batching sensitivity so small reorders don't collapse windows (but might raise unit cost)

 sre_oncall: I'm going to create an incident and page infra oncall to increase conntrack and check NAT appliance metrics. please post any repro steps/output here

 maria: repro notes: run bombard 50k short-lived TLS connections from one IP against our private egress (we used a test VM). saw conntrack fill in ~2m and KV eviction rate jump.

 leo: quick A/B test idea: pin the kernel selector to vector kernel on a single node pool, divert a small % of traffic (canary) and compare p50 and KV eviction. if it drops, that's strong evidence the fallback path is causing the perf regression

 infra-bot: incident created: INC-2026-0424 - private-eu-west-egress-conntrack-starvation (severity 2)

 tj: small config snippets we used for mitigation (applied to test nodes):

 ```bash
 # increase conntrack max
 sudo sysctl -w net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_max=524288
 sudo sysctl -w net.ipv4.ip_local_port_range="10240 60999"
 # decrease conntrack timeout for ESTABLISHED to remove stale entries faster (careful)
 sudo sysctl -w net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_tcp_timeout_established=86400
 ```

 ashok: also updated runtime toggles to force kernel selection: 
 ```json
 { "kernel_selector": "force_vectorized", "batching": { "min_window_ms": 6, "max_window_ms": 80 } }
 ```

 maria: after increasing conntrack_max and forcing kernel we saw p50 drop from ~180ms to ~45ms on canary and KV eviction rate normalized within 3 minutes. throughput recovered.

 leo: that suggests multiple contributors: conntrack exhaustion was causing egress failures/retransmits and also indirectly causing the runtime to hit slower code paths.

 sre_oncall: next steps from incident page: (1) roll conntrack_max change as cluster-level sysctl for private pools (2) schedule kernel-selector telemetry to surface fallback reasons (3) add egress connection pooling for tenants who make lots of short requests (4) add guard rails in autoscaler to consider conntrack pressure

 tj: I'll open a small RFC for (2) and (3) — we need tracing that tags requests which experienced kernel fallback so we can correlate with req logs

 maria: thanks all, will keep monitoring. ping me if you see another spike :thumbsup:

 deploy-bot: deploy completed: runtime-config-update canary -> applied to private-eu-west-1 at 02:44 UTC

 leo: nice follow-up: also let's add an e2e perf test that simulates short-lived TLS churn to prevent regressions where batching heuristics get tripped by kernel/kernel-path changes

 ashok: agreed. i'll add a test to the perf harness and a dashboard that shows kernel-selector fallback rate by node

 maria: resolved for now, tracking in INC-2026-0424 :white_check_mark:
